| 1 | **`EnforceCodeStyleInBuild` on every build** — most expensive; runs Roslyn style analyzers on every compilation | Removed entirely; use `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` in CI instead |
| 2 | **`GenerateDocumentationFile` always on** — XML doc generation on every dev build | Conditional on `Release` / `ContinuousIntegrationBuild` only |
| 3 | **`TreatWarningsAsErrors` on every build** — slows inner loop by forcing all warnings to be resolved | Conditional on `Release` / CI only |
| 4 | **Redundant `TargetFramework`** in all 5 `.csproj` files | Removed — already centralized in `Directory.Build.props` |
| 5 | **Redundant transitive `ProjectReference`s** — BusinessLogic→Common (via DataAccess), WebApi→DataAccess+Common (via BusinessLogic), Tests→all 4 (via WebApi) | Trimmed to minimal direct references |
| 6 | **Unnecessary x64/x86 solution platforms** — all mapped to AnyCPU anyway | Removed, keeping only `Debug|Any CPU` and `Release|Any CPU` |
| 7 | **Missing `.editorconfig`** — no style rule configuration | Added with style category set to `suggestion` severity |

### Result
- **Debug build**: ✅ succeeds in ~2s (was failing)
- **Release build**: ✅ succeeds in ~1.7s
- **Tests**: all 3 pass

### CI Recommendation
Add `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` as a separate CI step to enforce code style without penalizing build time.
